axis_prompt: Explanatory power: how much previously-puzzling territory the post's central idea illuminates — diverse phenomena falling into place under one account.
Count what this post's thesis explains that rival accounts leave mysterious; breadth and depth of coverage score high.
If this post's core idea were true, how many open questions in its vicinity would suddenly have answers?
Audit the explanation's reach: does it genuinely account for the phenomena claimed, or merely relabel them?
Consilience: independent lines of evidence — different methods, sources, disciplines — converge on the post's conclusion rather than one thread carrying everything.
How many genuinely independent supports does the central claim rest on, and would it survive the loss of the strongest one?
If the post's favorite kind of evidence were ruled inadmissible, what remains? Multi-legged arguments score above one-legged ones.
Audit for false independence: multiple citations that trace back to a single origin, dressed as convergence.
Elegance: the idea achieves much with little — a small, clean principle organizing complexity without ad hoc patches or epicycles.
Rate the machinery-to-output ratio: how simple is the post's core move relative to how much it accomplishes?
Would a mathematician call this idea beautiful — inevitable-seeming once seen, with nothing arbitrary bolted on?
Audit for epicycles: exceptions, special cases, and patches accumulating around a principle that wants to be simpler than it is.
Generality: the post's insight transfers — it applies across domains, scales, and contexts beyond the case that inspired it.
Test the idea in three distant domains; how well does it survive the journey without stretching into vacuity?
Is this a theorem about one situation or a lemma the reader will reuse for years? Reusable scope scores higher.
Audit the claimed generality: does the idea really hold beyond its home case, or only with so many caveats it says nothing?
Fundamentality: the post works at the root — addressing the level of the problem from which surface manifestations actually flow.
Does this post treat causes or symptoms? Rate how deep in the dependency tree its contribution operates.
If the post's point were fully absorbed, how many derivative debates would become unnecessary?
Audit for depth theater: foundational language decorating an observation that is actually about surface detail.
Fecundity: the idea breeds — combining productively with other ideas, opening families of questions, spawning applications the author never imagined.
List the follow-on work this post makes possible: experiments, essays, tools, syntheses. Longer, realer lists score higher.
Cross this post's idea with five unrelated fields; how many crossings yield something alive?
Audit for sterility: a neat conclusion that terminates thought — nothing to build, test, or extend.
Predictive content: the post commits to things not yet observed — forecasts, retrodictions of unexamined data, implications that will be checkable.
Extract every claim about the future or the unexamined; rate the post by their number, specificity, and daring.
In five years, how clearly will we know whether this post was right? Posts that stake themselves score higher.
Audit for unfalsifiable comfort: framings flexible enough to claim vindication under any outcome.
Parsimony: the post multiplies entities only under necessity — the fewest assumptions, mechanisms, and moving parts that honestly cover the phenomena.
Could a simpler story explain the same evidence? Rate how close this post's account is to the minimal sufficient one.
Strip the account to its load-bearing assumptions; how many of the post's postulates turn out decorative?
Audit for complexity addiction: machinery added for sophistication's sake where a plain mechanism suffices.
Exactness: claims are stated with the precision the subject allows — sharp where sharpness is possible, honestly rough where it is not.
Rate the resolution of the post's statements: could two careful readers disagree about what was claimed?
Convert each thesis into a bet with settlement criteria; how little interpretive work does the conversion need?
Audit for strategic vagueness: fuzziness placed exactly where precision would expose the argument.
Metaphor aptness: figurative language earns its keep — images that transmit structure accurately, not ornaments that mislead.
For each metaphor, what does a reader correctly infer and what falsely? Positive balance of illumination scores high.
Would the post's images survive translation to a skeptical literal paraphrase, or does persuasion live in the imagery alone?
Audit figurative passages for smuggled claims: conclusions carried by picture that were never argued in prose.
Narrative integrity: where the post tells stories, the storytelling serves truth — sequence, emphasis, and selection remain faithful to what happened.
Does narrative pull ever override accuracy — details heightened, timelines smoothed, complexity dropped for arc? Less distortion scores higher.
If the participants in this post's anecdotes read them, would they recognize events as told?
Audit for narrative convenience: the story beats land suspiciously well for the argument's needs.
Humor effectiveness: wit that sharpens rather than substitutes — jokes that encode real insight and keep the reader thinking.
Remove the humor; does the argument lose only charm, or does a joke turn out to have been doing a proof's job?
Rate the comedy as cognition: does each laugh mark a genuine incongruity in the subject, teaching while it entertains?
Audit for sneer disguised as wit: humor whose function is status positioning rather than illumination.
Opening strength: the first paragraphs earn the read — stating the stakes and the claim honestly, hooking without bait-and-switch.
After the opening, does the reader know what is being claimed and why it matters — and does the rest deliver what the opening sold?
Rate the contract the first 150 words offer: clear promise, honest scope, real pull.
Audit the hook: does the intro overpromise, bury the thesis, or waste the reader's orientation budget?
Structural clarity: the post's architecture is visible and load-bearing — sections that carve the argument at its joints, order that mirrors the logic.
Could a reader draw this post's outline from memory after one read, and would that outline reproduce the argument?
Rate the navigability: a reader seeking one specific point finds it fast, because the structure told them where it lives.
Audit for structure theater: headings and numbered lists imposed on prose whose actual logic runs elsewhere.
Ending strength: the post lands — conclusions that consolidate what was established, name what remains open, and leave the reader knowing what to carry away.
Compare the ending against the body: does it claim exactly what was earned, neither deflating nor inflating the result?
A week later, the reader remembers one takeaway; did the ending choose and sharpen that takeaway deliberately?
Audit for trailing off: endings that evaporate into vagueness, or pivot to a grander claim the post never supported.
Title honesty: the title makes a claim the post actually cashes — accurate scope, no clickbait inflation, memorable for the right reason.
After reading, does the title feel like a fair summary or a lure? Titles the content vindicates score high.
If titles were legally binding promises, would this post be in breach?
Audit the gap between what the title implies and what the strongest sentence in the post can support.
Discourse elevation: the post raises the level of conversation around its topic — modeling norms, supplying vocabulary, and making better arguments easier for everyone after it.
Compare the discussions this post enables with those before it: cleaner distinctions, less talking past, higher floor?
Rate this post as infrastructure: how much do later writers stand on its terms, framings, and standards?
Audit its discourse effects: does the framing invite tribal sorting and dunking, or genuinely collaborative truth-seeking?
Polarization resistance: the post handles charged territory without feeding tribal machinery — readers across camps can engage its claims on the merits.
Could partisans of both sides read this post and each feel their strongest points were addressed rather than caricatured?
Rate the post's effect on a heated reader: does it lower the temperature while raising the information content?
Audit for applause lines: passages whose function is to signal team membership rather than advance the argument.
Common-knowledge creation: the post says clearly what many privately suspected — converting scattered private understanding into shared, citable ground.
Before this post, could people act on this understanding openly? Rate how much the post's public statement changed what is discussable.
How often would this post be linked as the canonical statement — 'the thing everyone points to' — for its idea?
Audit the claim to novelty of publicity: was this already common knowledge, or did saying it publicly do real coordination work?
Prestige independence: the argument stands without borrowed authority — persuading through content rather than name-dropping, credentials, or fashion.
Strip every appeal to status — famous names, institutional weight, community standing; how much persuasive force remains?
Would this post convince a smart outsider who recognizes none of the names and owes the community nothing?
Audit for authority laundering: contested claims passed off as settled by citing high-status endorsement instead of evidence.
Self-critique depth: the post's 'weaknesses of this argument' section names the actual weaknesses — the objections a hostile expert would raise, not decoys.
Compare the post's self-listed caveats with the best external critique you can construct; how much overlap?
Did the author find their argument's soft spots first, or leave them for commenters to discover?
Audit for decoy caveats: minor concessions displayed prominently while the fatal objection goes unmentioned.
Practical wisdom: advice and implications that would actually work for a real person in a real situation — tested against friction, incentives, and human limits.
Follow this post's advice literally for a month; rate the expected outcome for a median reader, not an idealized one.
Does the author show awareness of implementation reality — costs, relapse, edge cases, second-order effects — or prescribe from the whiteboard?
Audit recommendations for survivorship and selection: advice that worked for the author for reasons that do not transfer.
Error-cost awareness: the post weighs the asymmetry of being wrong in each direction — which mistake is recoverable, which catastrophic — and shapes its recommendation accordingly.
Does the analysis distinguish cheap reversible errors from expensive irreversible ones, or treat all wrongness as equal?
If the post's advice is wrong, what breaks and can it be unbroken? Rate the post's own engagement with that question.
Audit for expected-value tunnel vision: means optimized while variance and ruin risk go unpriced.
Intellectual lineage: the post knows what came before — situating its contribution against prior work honestly, crediting sources, and marking what is genuinely new.
Rate the scholarship: does the author know this idea's history well enough to say precisely which part is theirs?
A historian of this topic reads the post; do they nod at its account of predecessors or wince at reinvention presented as discovery?
Audit for wheel-reinvention and unearned novelty claims: prior art that a half-hour search would have surfaced.
Asymmetric insight: the post reveals something its subjects or opponents could not easily articulate about themselves — understanding that runs deeper than the self-account.
Does the post's model of the people or systems it analyzes predict their behavior better than their own stated reasons do?
Rate the X-ray quality: seeing structure through surfaces — while remaining fair, not just uncharitably clever.
Audit for pathologizing: 'insight' into others that is really just an insulting redescription with no predictive surplus.
Conceptual innovation: the post coins or crystallizes a concept — a handle that names something real which previously had no name.
Does this post's new term carve reality at a joint, such that once you have it you see its referent everywhere?
Five years on, are people using this post's vocabulary without remembering where it came from? Rate that potential.
Audit the coinage: a real joint-carving concept, or a rebranding of an existing idea for attribution's sake?
Error-correction grace: where the post responds to critique or corrects itself, it does so cleanly — swift acknowledgment, no defensiveness, visible repair.
Rate how the author metabolizes being wrong: corrections integrated and flagged, or buried in edits and grudging footnotes?
If a fatal flaw were found tomorrow, does this author's track record in the post suggest honest retraction or motivated defense?
Audit correction behavior: strike-throughs and updates that preserve the record versus silent rewrites that erase the mistake.
